answer: No, not by default. The 3-minute SLA is the first test: micro-batch with a trigger well under it (e.g. 10-30 s, p99 far below 3 min) meets it, so a record-at-a-time engine is only needed if the SLA is shorter than micro-batch's tail latency (about 1-2 s or less). Second, when both meet the SLA, the team decides: the operations group already runs the batch engine, so micro-batch on that existing cluster, with the same code and on-call rotation, is the choice. Record-at-a-time would add a second runtime to operate for latency the SLA does not require.
